label: Exponential improvement continuing
rationale: The best 80% METR time horizon reached 32.3 min (GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, Nov 2025), growing at a ~7-month doubling rate long-run and possibly ~4 months in 2024–2025. Caveat: METR's RCT found experienced developers 19% slower with AI tools, so benchmark gains do not yet translate to real-world productivity.

label: Approaching
rationale: No verified case meets the strict criteria (solo founder, $10M ARR, <10 hrs/week oversight); Magnific AI is at $10M ARR with 2 people and several AI-heavy solo founders are at ~$3M ARR. Current examples show AI as a coding accelerator, not an autonomous business operator.

label: Distant
rationale: The largest confirmed AI-generated patch merged into Linux is ~50 lines (in 6.15, undisclosed and buggy), 200× short of the 10k-line target. Major projects (Gentoo, NetBSD, Git, QEMU) ban or restrict AI code, and AI is adopted only in auxiliary maintenance roles.

label: Distant (structurally blocked)
rationale: All major journals (Nature, Science, Cell, JAMA/Lancet/BMJ) prohibit AI authorship, so the barrier is policy and accountability rather than capability. The closest approach, Sakana AI Scientist-v2's ICLR workshop paper, was accepted and then withdrawn.

label: Ahead: 80% horizon 185.9 min (Apr 2026); doubling ~4.1 mo in 2 yrs vs ~7 mo benchmark (tier 3)
rationale: The release-cohort METR 80% time horizon rose from 4.42 min (frontier at 2024-09-30) to 185.91 min (Claude Mythos Preview early, released 2026-04-07), a 42x gain over the 2-year window across 9 new frontier points: a log-linear fit gives a doubling time of 4.1 months (95% CI 3.4-5.1), and the endpoint ratio gives 4.45 months. That beats the tier-3 benchmark of sustaining METR's long-run ~7-month doubling, and it is faster than the previous window 2022-09-30..2024-09-30 (0.26 -> 4.42 min, endpoint doubling 5.9 months), so the status is green (Ahead). The result survives dropping the latest, wide-CI point (4.4 months), and it already absorbs the ~6 months since April 2026 with no new frontier.

label: Progressing: solo AI-heavy firms ~$3-3.5M ARR; <10 h/week oversight unevidenced; ETA 5-10 yrs
rationale: No verified achievement event shows a single-person company at $10M ARR with <10 hours/week of oversight. The closest solo cases are about $3M (Pieter Levels, corrected record) and Base44's $3.5M ARR before its $80M exit (legacy); the $10M-plus small-team cases are 2-person Magnific or the largely pre-AI 1-person BuiltWith (legacy, non-primary), with no oversight data. That is measurable progress on the revenue half at ~1/3 of the target, and OpenView finds AI-native startups 8x likelier to reach $10M ARR within 12 months, but nothing evidences the <10 h/week clause, and there is no programme or non-proponent corroboration that would support a <=5-year ETA. The credible ETA is 5-10 years, so the status is yellow.

label: Distant: one LLM-written patch merged (Linux 6.15, human-submitted); no path to a 10k-line AI patch
rationale: The only verified precursor is LWN's report that a patch merged for Linux 6.15 was entirely LLM-written and posted without disclosure; re-verification removed the earlier size and bug details, and it was human-submitted. There is no series on the size of accepted AI-generated patches to extrapolate and no funded programme aiming at AI-submitted large patches. Torvalds positions AI for maintaining, not writing, kernel code, and critical-infra projects ban AI code (Gentoo, QEMU) or require a human in the loop (LLVM), which cuts against an 'AI-submitted' patch. With no evidenced path, the status is red (Distant).

label: Blocked: Nature/Science bar AI authorship (policy); best precursor an ICLR workshop paper, withdrawn
rationale: The milestone requires AI credited as primary author in Nature/Science, and both journals' policies bar AI authorship: 'LLMs do not currently satisfy our authorship criteria' and 'AI tools cannot be authors' (legacy record, used as context). That is a structural policy block whatever the technical readiness. The best verified precursor is Sakana's AI Scientist-v2 paper, which passed peer review at an ICLR 2025 workshop but was withdrawn before publication because the community had not decided whether to publish AI-generated manuscripts. Recognitions such as the 2024 chemistry Nobel went to humans, so no evidence moves the block, and the status is red (Blocked).

label: Progressing: best AI-era solo firms ~$3M/yr (30% of $10M); <10 h/wk oversight unproven; ETA ~2030
rationale: No verified case shows a one-person company at $10M ARR with <10 h/week of oversight. The best AI-era solo figures are ~$3M (Pieter Levels; HeadshotPro, legacy), and a pre-AI solo firm already exceeds $10M (BuiltWith, legacy), so the binding clause is oversight. It maps onto the METR 80% horizon: about a work-week (2,400 min) of autonomous work is needed vs 185.91 min today, 12.9x or 3.7 doublings plus ~1.6 for messy business operations, which at a 5-month doubling and a 1.5-year ramp to disclosure gives p50 ~2030 (p10 2028, p90 2034). The median is within 5 years, but there is no funded programme, no precursor at relevant scale and no independent corroboration of the oversight clause, so the status is yellow, not green.

eta.calc: Revenue clause: best AI-era solo ~$3M (Levels, 2025-01-01-pieter-levels-3m-arr-rv; HeadshotPro $3M ARR, legacy tinyteams) -> 10/3 = 3.3x (1.74 doublings); pre-AI 1-person BuiltWith $14M/yr (legacy) shows the level is attainable. Ramp check: AI-native startups 8x likelier to hit $10M ARR within 12 months (OpenView); Base44 $3.5M run-rate within ~6 months (not evidenced as one-person).
eta.cruxes: Earlier: a verified 1-person company at >=$10M ARR disclosing low founder hours; an 80% horizon >= ~8 h by mid-2027; AI-era solo businesses passing $5M. Later: horizon doubling slowing past ~8 months; agent reliability failures in customer-facing operations (cf. 95% of GenAI pilots falling short); legal/compliance duties that need human hours; oversight hours never disclosed, so the milestone cannot be verified.

label: Progressing: one LLM-written patch merged (Linux 6.15); 10k lines ~484x the 80% horizon; ETA ~2031
rationale: The only verified precursor is a fully LLM-written patch merged for Linux 6.15, human-submitted and of unstated size, but the milestone ties to the METR 80% horizon, which grew 42x in two years. A substantive 10k-line patch series is ~1,500 h of expert work, 484x today's 185.91-min horizon: at 8.9 doublings plus one for real-world messiness and a 5-month doubling, the capability arrives ~2030, and a 1-year review floor gives p50 ~2031 (p10 2028, p90 2038). Gentoo, QEMU and NetBSD bar AI code and LLVM requires a human in the loop, but Linux has no ban and 'or equivalent critical infra' needs only one accepting project, so this is a risk rather than a structural block. The path lacks a programme, a precursor at scale and corroboration, so the status is yellow (Progressing).

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the driver it is tied to (METR 80% horizon) with median ETA <= 10 years; the path lacks green's conditions (no funded programme, no precursor at relevant scale, no corroboration); not blocked, because no ban covers Linux and 'or equivalent critical infra' allows any accepting project

eta.method: driver trend (METR 80% horizon, exponential) + structural floor (review/acceptance of a 10k-line series); reference class cross-check

eta.cruxes: Earlier: an agent-authored multi-thousand-line series merged into any critical project; kernel docs (Hansen's generated-content guidelines) explicitly allowing agent-submitted patches with disclosure; an 80% horizon >= 1 work-week by 2027. Later: the kernel or other projects requiring human submitters / Signed-off-by for AI code; horizon doubling slowing past ~8 months; mergeable-quality rates staying far below benchmark pass rates.

basis.path: Driver: METR 80% horizon (4.42 -> 185.91 min, 2024-10..2026-04), the RUBRIC §4.1's own mapping for an AI-written 10k-line patch. basis.path: Reading: 'AI-submitted' = an AI system did the engineering and is the disclosed submitter (sends the series, answers review, revises); a human may set the goal and start the agent but does not direct the code. '10k+ lines diff' = one accepted contribution (patch or series merged as one feature) with >= 10,000 changed lines of substantive code. 'Equivalent critical infra' = foundational OSS with comparable review: LLVM/GCC, glibc, CPython, OpenSSL, Kubernetes, Node.js core. eta.cruxes: 1) Spacing of the tiers above the main track (structural): a fully AI paper accepted in a top field journal (e.g. a refereed AI-generated proof) -> shrinking/equal (up to -2.0 yr); none while the blended horizon passes ~50 h -> growing (+2.7). 2) Autonomy deficit m: a fully AI-generated main-track acceptance at blended <= 4 h (about early 2027) -> m near 0 (-0.7); shadow-eval-type failures of models measured at >= 1-4 h (e.g. the announced GPT-5.6 Sol / Opus 5 / Fable 5 follow-ups), read through the assumed transfer -> m > 0.73 (+0.4) to m >= 2.5 (+1.4). 3) Rate: next ECI/RLI points; METR's long-run pace +2.6 yr. 4) Rung dating: acceptance dates of future rungs; a measured Nature submission-to-acceptance time matters only under the capability-dated alternative (+0.5). 5) Failures (assumed): AI research stuck at co-produced level while horizons grow -> novelty up (8%: p90 null).
eta.assumes: the journal would credit an AI as primary author once it clearly did the work (today Nature and Science bar AI authorship); it tracks AI research capability, not editorial policy.

basis.path: Reading (framework details): the flagship Nature or Science, a research article; AI-generated = the AI poses the question, designs and analyses the work and writes the paper; humans may fund, provide compute, run lab protocols as directed and submit, but contribute no ideas or text; primary author = first/lead author. Alternative (sensitivity, -1.76 yr): a Nature-family or top field journal suffices. Driver: shared task-horizon at 80% (owner decision), blended domain (research spans code and analysis plus writing, figures and judgement); the mapping is a venue ladder read at acceptance dates (so review time is inside it and no lag is added): the workshop-to-main-track spacing is fitted on two reached rungs (the workshop rung's remote component backcast with its uncertainty), the autonomy deficit of the main-track rung is an assumed half-normal (the shadow evaluations tested Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 Sol, whose horizons are at or below 0.598 h and 0.990 h, so they bound it only through an assumed transfer, a sensitivity), and the tiers above are labelled structural spacing scenarios, not a fitted link. Precursors: AI Scientist-v2 workshop paper (withdrawn; reported in Nature 2026-03); Agents4Science AI-first-author papers; Robin and Co-Scientist (AI-generated hypotheses and analyses in human-authored Nature papers); Sakana's co-produced ALIFE 2026 oral (accepted 2026-06-07); OpenAI's 722 AI math manuscripts (unrefereed) and contested Navier-Stokes claim. Counter-signals: shadow evaluations (Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 Sol agents failed NeurIPS-level open questions).
blockers: Assumed gate, real state: Nature Portfolio and Science bar AI authorship (2025-01-01-journals-prohibit-ai-authorship-rv); Springer Nature's risk-based policy (2026-09-10-springer-nature-risk-based-ai-policy) keeps accountability non-delegable and classes AI generating hypotheses, analyses or conclusions without human oversight and assigning authorship to AI as not permitted. This does not delay the ETA (RUBRIC §4.2), but 'achieved' needs an AI credited as primary author

basis.path: Reading (wording unchanged): one owner, no employees, no contractors running operations (incidental legal/accounting allowed); ARR = recurring revenue annualized, summed over all businesses the person owns and runs (one-off sales and pass-through excluded); oversight = all human time running them, < 10 h/week averaged over a quarter at >= $10M ARR. Two conditions, the later binds (revenue in 45% of draws): revenue from the solo-revenue ladder (Polsia $4.64M recurring in May 2026 from an anonymous analysis of its dashboard; Levels $2.4-3.0M total revenue with an assumed recurring share; paces structural, not fitted); oversight from a capability gate on the shared driver task-horizon at 80% success in the blended domain (owner decision, audit 2026-10-16-reliability-level; RUBRIC 4.1 step 3: < 10 h/week over a quarter is sustained unattended operation; 50% is a labelled sensitivity, -0.45 yr), H = L x c: L = 226 work hours per oversight hour from the oversight budget and SaaS Capital ARR per FTE (sourced), c the owner's minutes per autonomous run, a labelled structural scenario range (2/11/46 min); the mapping of horizon onto oversight hours is assumed, not measured; port leverage and Vending-Bench are analogues used only as cross-checks.

rationale: Judged as if maintainers took openly AI-submitted patches on merit. eta.assumes: maintainers judge an openly AI-submitted patch on its merits (no blanket ban on AI-written code, no human-submitter rule); it tracks AI engineering capability, not project policy.

basis.path: Reading: 'AI-submitted' = an AI system did the engineering and is the disclosed submitter (sends the series, answers review, revises); a human may set the goal and start the agent but does not direct the code. '10k+ lines diff' = one accepted contribution (patch or series merged as one feature) with >= 10,000 changed lines of substantive code. 'Equivalent critical infra' = foundational OSS with comparable review: LLVM/GCC, glibc, CPython, OpenSSL, Kubernetes, Node.js core. Alternative reading (sensitivity, definition crux): openly AI-written, human-directed series count once the human-submitter rule is assumed away; under it the Node.js commit (2026-05-23-nodejs-merges-10k-line-ai-assisted-vfs) may already qualify, else 2027.26 (-2.29 yr). The size threshold is already passed by AI-written human-submitted work (Ladybird, Bun, Node.js); the remaining gap is autonomy. Driver: shared task-horizon at 80% success (owner decision, audit 2026-10-16-reliability-level; RUBRIC 4.1 step 3 as clarified 2026-10-16: AI submissions to maintainers flooded by AI slop burn goodwill when they fail, so they cannot be repeated freely and need the reliable level; 50% is a labelled sensitivity, p50 2028), software domain; mapping H_req = E x 2^x, where x1 is the horizon's definition (not a calibration), E (effort of a qualifying contribution) a labelled scenario range around the one sourced accepted example (Ladybird) and x labelled oracle-lower / messiness scenarios from measured gaps; none of these is measured on maintainer review.

eta.cruxes: 1) Spacing of the tiers above the main track (structural): a fully AI paper accepted in a top field journal (e.g. a refereed AI-generated proof) -> shrinking/equal (up to -2.0 yr); none while the blended horizon passes ~50 h -> growing (+2.7). 2) Autonomy deficit m: a fully AI-generated main-track acceptance at blended <= 4 h (about early 2027) -> m near 0 (-0.7); shadow-eval-type failures of models measured at >= 1-4 h (e.g. the announced GPT-5.6 Sol / Opus 5 / Fable 5 follow-ups), read through the assumed transfer -> m > 0.73 (+0.4) to m >= 2.5 (+1.4). 3) Rate: next ECI/RLI points; METR's long-run pace +2.6 yr. 4) Rung dating: acceptance dates of future rungs; a measured Nature submission-to-acceptance time matters only under the capability-dated alternative (+0.5). 5) Failures (assumed): AI research stuck at co-produced level while horizons grow -> novelty up (8%: p90 null). 6) Precursor series ai-paper-venue-tier-max: a tier-2 row (fully AI main track) -> m small (toward -0.7); a tier-3 row -> shrinking/equal spacing (up to -2.0); still tier 1 with fully-AI submissions rejected on merit while blended passes ~4-8 h -> m large (+1.0 to +1.4).
eta.assumes: the journal would credit an AI as primary author once it clearly did the work (today Nature and Science bar AI authorship); it tracks AI research capability, not editorial policy.

basis.path: Reading (framework details): the flagship Nature or Science, a research article; AI-generated = the AI poses the question, designs and analyses the work and writes the paper; humans may fund, provide compute, run lab protocols as directed and submit, but contribute no ideas or text; primary author = first/lead author. Alternative (sensitivity, -1.62 yr): a Nature-family or top field journal suffices. Driver: shared task-horizon at 80% success (owner decision, audit 2026-10-16-reliability-level; RUBRIC 4.1 step 3 as clarified 2026-10-16: a paper submitted to editors and referees flooded by AI slop burns goodwill when it fails, so attempts cannot be repeated freely; 50% is a labelled sensitivity, +0.02 yr), blended domain (research spans code and analysis plus writing, figures and judgement); the mapping is a venue ladder read at acceptance dates (so review time is inside it and no lag is added): the workshop-to-main-track spacing is fitted on two reached rungs (the workshop rung's remote component backcast with its uncertainty), the autonomy deficit of the main-track rung is an assumed half-normal (the shadow evaluations tested Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 Sol, whose horizons are at or below 0.598 h and 0.990 h, so they bound it only through an assumed transfer, a sensitivity), and the tiers above are labelled structural spacing scenarios, not a fitted link. Precursors: AI Scientist-v2 workshop paper (withdrawn; reported in Nature 2026-03); Agents4Science AI-first-author papers; Robin and Co-Scientist (AI-generated hypotheses and analyses in human-authored Nature papers); Sakana's co-produced ALIFE 2026 oral (accepted 2026-06-07); OpenAI's 722 AI math manuscripts (unrefereed) and contested Navier-Stokes claim. Counter-signals: shadow evaluations (Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 Sol agents failed NeurIPS-level open questions).
blockers: Assumed gate, real state: Nature Portfolio and Science bar AI authorship (2025-01-01-journals-prohibit-ai-authorship-rv); Springer Nature's risk-based policy (2026-09-10-springer-nature-risk-based-ai-policy) keeps accountability non-delegable and classes AI generating hypotheses, analyses or conclusions without human oversight and assigning authorship to AI as not permitted. This does not delay the ETA (RUBRIC §4.2), but 'achieved' needs an AI credited as primary author
